task.title: Fall back when the validation cache WAL pragmas fail, and pin the journal mode
task.description:
Deferred from PR #36 (WB-01KYT6XA289VV2QNGTXZG9S31H, "Bound full history validation time and peak memory growth").

internal/historyvalidation/cache.go:539-540 adds `_pragma=journal_mode(WAL)` and `_pragma=synchronous(NORMAL)` to every validation cache DSN, unconditionally and with no fallback.

modernc.org/sqlite applies each `_pragma` with c.exec and returns the error verbatim (sqlite@v1.54.0/sqlite.go:230-236), so a pragma that fails fails the connection open, which fails OpenCache, which fails `workbook validate` outright. WAL requires shared-memory (-shm mmap) support, which NFS and SMB mounts commonly lack, and converting an existing file can also return SQLITE_BUSY while another connection holds it. Scenario: a developer whose repo lives on an NFS-mounted home directory runs `workbook validate` and it now errors at cache open where the rollback journal previously worked.

The cache is disposable by construction - rebuildDatabase already regenerates it whenever it is unusable (cache.go:579) - so degrading to the previous journal mode when the pragma errors costs nothing but a slower run. Suggested shape: attempt the WAL DSN, and on a pragma failure at open, retry once without the journal_mode and synchronous pragmas.

Second, smaller half: nothing pins the pragmas. Deleting both lines leaves the entire suite green, even though the PR body and docs/performance provenance both cite WAL as part of the fix. A test that opens a cache and asserts `PRAGMA journal_mode` returns wal and `PRAGMA synchronous` returns 1 would stop a silent revert. (The pragmas do take effect today: validation.sqlite header byte 18 == 2, and validationSidecarBytes == 0 at every measured depth in the storage family, since sidecars are cleaned up at cache.go:589-593.)

Deferred because the change is correct on every supported local filesystem and the failure requires a network mount; it is a robustness gap on an untested platform rather than a defect in the measured path.
